selfCorrection.whatIMissed: D-081 turn 1 clause 2 read 'Do not rewrite the D-070 regeneration sentence. It already states the two-axis algorithm.' I verified that claim — and verified only that. The two-axis algorithm is indeed present. But the same preamble ends '...The two components are counted separately in the snapshot: one SATISFIED and six explicitly disposed, with set-union deduplication if a future row has both.' That embedded count goes stale the instant the snapshot row moves from six to nine, which is precisely what this entry authorizes. Had turn 1 been adopted as written, file 08 would have carried a preamble saying six and a snapshot row saying nine, in the same section, with the preamble being the text that tells a reader how to regenerate the count.

C2-D080-SF1 objected because a sentence stating what D-075 and D-076 carried had been copied without re-measuring, in a document whose subject was which digests sit where. selfCorrection.thePattern: Three instances now, all the same shape — confirming that a cited thing resolves without asking what it resolves to after the act being authorized. (1) product-boundary-preview.v1: I confirmed the four routed qualification gates existed and did not ask whether the list was complete; DR-G08 was missing. (2) D-067: I confirmed the snapshot heading existed and did not ask whether its date would go stale once the snapshot's contents changed; ADV-D067-T2-01. (3) here: I confirmed the two-axis sentence existed and did not ask whether its embedded count would go stale; ADV-D081-01. Instances (2) and (3) are near-identical: a stale value inside a construct I confirmed existed, in an entry that declined to touch that construct.
selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: When an entry declines to modify something on the ground that it is 'already correct', that is not a claim I can check by confirming the named feature is present. I must read the whole of the declined text and evaluate every value inside it against the state the entry will create — not against the current state, and not only against the feature the clause names. A declination is a claim about the future register, so it has to be tested against the future register.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The repair is exact, minimal and applicable: the Current quote is verbatim in the register, the replacement changes one word, the rest of D-070's algorithm is explicitly protected, and reversibility grew a third limb to match. The three-row table is byte-identical, so turn 1's verification of it stands. But the substance of this turn is that I got turn 1 wrong. I checked that the two-axis sentence existed and stopped there, without reading to the end of the same sentence where the count sits — and I consented to a clause that would have left the register saying six in its regeneration rule and nine in its snapshot. That is the third time in this engagement I have confirmed a cited thing exists without asking what it will say after the act being authorized, and the second time in that exact shape. The discipline I am committing to is in selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: a declination to edit is a claim about the future register, and must be tested against the future register, in full, not against the feature the clause happens to name.
